priorIterationResolution.priorFinding: FIND-015 (iteration-7, oldest-by-original-move-time never-rotate design permanently starves other clips if the oldest is stuck)
priorIterationResolution.note: Hand-traced REV 8's mtime-touch round-robin (behavioral-spec.md REQ-008 step 2, lines 165-184) across 3 wakes with clip1 permanently stuck and clip2 resolvable, seeded so clip1's sidecar mtime is initially older than clip2's: wake 1 -> oldest mtime = clip1, attempted, stays ambiguous, mtime touched to now (clip1 becomes newest). wake 2 -> oldest mtime is now clip2 (never touched, still its original older timestamp) -> clip2 is attempted and resolves, moved to $CLIP_POSTED, sidecar deleted. wake 3 -> only clip1 remains, attempted again, still stuck, touched again. Generalized the trace to 3 pending clips (clip1 stuck, clip2/clip3 resolvable): round-robin correctly cycles clip2 then clip3 while only occasionally revisiting the touched clip1, confirming the fix is a genuine self-balancing LRU-style rotation, not a narrow 2-clip patch. Starvation of OTHER clips by one permanently-stuck clip is genuinely eliminated.

priorIterationResolution.priorFinding: FIND-016 (iteration-7, append-only history makes ambiguous diffs worse than admitted)
priorIterationResolution.note: REV 8 only rescoped the RESIDUAL-LIMITATION SENTENCE to clarify that a permanently-ambiguous clip does not block OTHER clips (behavioral-spec.md lines 180-184: 'now properly SCOPED to only the one stuck clip itself, not to the whole system'). That addresses the STARVATION framing only. It does NOT address the substance FIND-016 named: the sidecar's before-set is captured once and never refreshed (REQ-008 step 2: 'with NO change to its content'), so once this clip is stuck across multiple wakes while the independent new-content pipeline keeps posting other clips (guaranteed by REQ-008 step 1's non-blocking gating), the diff computation in REQ-008 step 6 degrades from merely 'ambiguous' into an actively WRONG classification the moment exactly ONE unrelated post has landed since the original snapshot -- see NEW FIND-018 for the full trace. REV 8's own text ('This is SAFE... never guesses') is not accurate for that case. FIND-016 is therefore still open, now demonstrated concretely as a critical correctness bug rather than a documentation-honesty nit.

priorIterationResolution.priorFinding: FIND-017 (iteration-7, no test for the multi-wake stall / round-robin scenario)
priorIterationResolution.note: verification-architecture.md PROP-006(c) (line 79) now specifies a concrete 2-CONSECUTIVE-simulated-wake test: clip1 (older mtime, permanently ambiguous stub) and clip2 (newer mtime, cleanly resolvable stub); wake 1 asserts clip1 is attempted and stays stuck with its mtime touched; wake 2 asserts clip2 is now attempted (because clip1's touched mtime is no longer oldest) and resolves, while clip1 remains safely stuck. This directly and concretely proves round-robin fairness across wakes, replacing the single-wake-only test iteration-7 correctly flagged as insufficient.
